idea.body: Add or subtract a polynomial by combining only the terms that match. A term matches another when it has the same variable raised to the same exponent. (3x^2 + 2x) + (x^2 - 5x) combines the two x^2 terms and the two x terms separately, giving 4x^2 - 3x. Subtracting works the same way, but first flip the sign of every term being subtracted. (5x + 3) - (2x - 4) becomes (5x + 3) + (-2x + 4), which combines to 3x + 7. A term with no match, like a lone constant, simply carries through unchanged.

steps: Subtracting a polynomial flips the sign of every one of its terms.

ways.name: Line up like terms
ways.when: Use this default method for adding or subtracting any polynomials.
steps: Match terms with the same variable and exponent: the x^2 terms, the x terms, the constants.
ways.trap: Combining terms with different exponents, like an x^2 term with an x term.

ways.name: Stack the polynomials in columns
ways.when: Use this when the polynomials are long and columns keep the terms straight.
steps: Write the two polynomials one under the other, in matching columns for x^2, x and the constant.
Flip the sign of every term in the polynomial being subtracted: -4x^2, +3x, -2.
Add straight down the x^2 column: 7 + (-4) = 3.
Add down the x column: 1 + 3 = 4. Add the constant column: -5 + (-2) = -7.
ways.trap: Writing a term in the wrong column when a polynomial is missing a matching term.

ways.name: Tiles that cancel
ways.when: Use this when a term looks like it might disappear after subtracting.
steps: Picture each term as a tile: 4x tiles and constant tiles.
Subtracting flips every tile in (4x + 5) to its opposite: -4x and -5.
The 4x tile and the new -4x tile cancel to zero.
The constants do not cancel: -9 and -5 combine to -14.
ways.trap: Cancelling tiles that are not actually the same size, like an x tile against a constant.
